verdict: The connected cut-group edge-transitivity sufficiency target passes source scope, current-primary and full numbered/source-alias comparison in this bounded audit.
findings: Physical 15 and 86 define weakly norming on bounded symmetric real measurable functions on the single square. The standalone absolute-value integral and quotient modulo almost-everywhere equality preserve that convention, instead of replacing it by an arbitrary nonsymmetric two-probability-space bigraph kernel.

Physical 91 explicitly starts the cut-involution definition with connected H, then requires a fixed-vertex cut and a partition into disjoint exchanged halves with no crossing edge. For a nontrivial cut the halves are nonempty. Root connectedness therefore follows the standing definition and is not an invented stronger hypothesis. All valid half choices contribute the same underlying cut involution group.

Physical 125 Conjecture 6.42 asks sufficiency of edge transitivity under the cut involution group without a percolating-sequence condition. Source Conjecture 6.43 is the separate converse and is not silently bundled into this recommendation.

Coregliano arXiv:2408.14257v1, whose body date is August 24, 2026, retains the stronger cut-percolation sufficiency conjecture. Theorem 1.2(v) also requires every symmetrically fold-stable colouring to be monochromatic; that extra hypothesis is not proved from edge transitivity. It does not close the source sufficiency target. Known ordinary automorphism-edge-transitivity necessity has the opposite direction and a different group.

The connected graph convention also aligns graph cut involutions with bipartition-preserving folds: a nontrivial cut has a fixed vertex, and an automorphism of a connected bipartite graph fixing a vertex preserves each side. No change to the source symmetric-kernel target is needed.

relationships: Q4994 asks for a vertex-transitive locally finite graph with every automorphism fixing some vertex, not a graph-norm property or edge transitivity of the generated cut group. Q2931 asks virtual specialness for groups generated by involutions with median Cayley graph. Neither has the integral-norm sufficiency predicate.

Q3581 counts Euclidean distance realizations for finite planar point sets; its Euclidean norm is unrelated to the homomorphism-density functional. Q2346 concerns Fock-space Toeplitz operator zero products. Q338 concerns stochastic game value convergence on transitive graphs.

Q1558 and Q263 concern edge partitions into trees/linear forests; Q1463 deletion saturation and Q1664 locally distinguishing edge weights. None quantifies bounded symmetric kernels and cut-involution groups. Q5038 classifies maximal subgroups of rooted-tree groups, not graph norming.
